title: Azure Service Bus Basics
description: Explore Azure Service Bus queues and topics for enterprise messaging in cloud-native .NET applications.

data.text: Azure Service Bus is a fully managed enterprise message broker provided by Microsoft Azure. It supports queues for point-to-point communication and topics with subscriptions for publish-subscribe scenarios. It is widely used in .NET and enterprise applications for reliable, transactional messaging.

A Service Bus queue delivers messages to a single consumer group. A topic expands this model by allowing multiple subscriptions. Each subscription receives a copy of every message published to the topic. Subscriptions can include filters, SQL rules, and actions, making topics a powerful tool for event broadcasting.

data.title: Use Topics for Event Routing
data.text: Topics with subscriptions and filter rules let you route the same event to multiple downstream systems without the publisher knowing about them. Each subscription acts as a virtual queue for a specific consumer group.

Service Bus sessions enable first-in-first-out (FIFO) processing within a session identifier. Messages in the same session are processed by a single consumer at a time, preserving order. This is useful for scenarios like per-user order processing where all messages for a given user must be handled sequentially.

data.title: Premium vs Standard Tiers
data.text: Premium tier offers dedicated resources, higher throughput, and geo-disaster recovery. Standard tier is cost-effective for development and low-volume workloads. Choose Premium for production SLAs above 99.9 percent.

items.question: Should I use Service Bus or Storage Queues?
items.answer: Use Service Bus for enterprise scenarios requiring transactions, sessions, duplicate detection, and pub/sub. Use Storage Queues for simple, lightweight point-to-point messaging at massive scale.

items.question: What is the message size limit?
items.answer: Standard tier limits messages to 256 KB. Premium tier supports up to 100 MB with partitioned entities or 1 GB with express entities.

items.question: How does Azure guarantee message durability?
items.answer: Service Bus stores messages redundantly across Azure Storage. In Premium tier, messages are stored on SSDs for sub-millisecond latency.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Queues deliver messages to a single consumer group
Topics with subscriptions enable publish-subscribe patterns
Sessions provide FIFO ordering within a session identifier
Premium tier offers higher throughput and dedicated resources
data.takeaway: Azure Service Bus is a mature enterprise broker; use queues for point-to-point and topics for event broadcasting.

data.title: Hands-on: Create a Service Bus Queue
data.description: Create an Azure Service Bus Standard namespace, add a queue named 'orders', and send a JSON message from a .NET console application. Verify the message appears in the Azure Portal Service Bus Explorer.
steps: Create a Service Bus Standard namespace in the Azure Portal
Add a queue named 'orders' with max size 1 GB
Write a .NET console app that sends a message and prints the MessageId
Open Service Bus Explorer in the portal and confirm the message count
data.expectedOutcome: You have a working Service Bus queue with a producer that successfully sends and a consumer that receives messages.
